title: Scaffold the Bun/TypeScript ward CLI: envelope, exit codes, safe errors, manifest, instructions
description: Spec §8 and §13. The skeleton every later command plugs into: fleet {schemaVersion, kind, data} envelope, semantic exit codes 0-7, errors on stderr with stable safe codes that never echo arguments, a manifest-driven parser, `ward manifest --json` and `ward instructions [topic]` (neither unlocks a vault), and an `npm run check` equivalent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `ward manifest --json` and `ward instructions` run without touching ~/.ward/
An unknown option or usage error carrying a sentinel value exits 2 and the sentinel appears in neither stdout nor stderr (first slice of T09)

plan: 1. package.json (@opum-ai/ward, private until release), tsconfig, biome, pinned devDeps matching quest-cli (biome 2.5.8, @types/bun 1.3.14, typescript 7.0.2); no runtime deps
2. src/contract: result/error envelopes, exit codes 0-7, WardError with static safe messages only (no input field, never interpolates argv)
3. src/contract/manifest: command definitions (args, flags, kind, mutates, admin, outputSensitivity, exitCodes)
4. src/cli: manifest-driven argv parser that reports positions not values; top-level catch maps any unexpected throw to a generic uncaught error
5. manifest, instructions [topic], help commands; nothing resolves or touches ~/.ward
6. tests: envelope/exit contract, sentinel non-echo (T09 first slice), HOME sandbox proves no ~/.ward created; subprocess smoke of the entry
7. check script = typecheck + lint + format + layer check + test
implementationNotes: Parser is hand-written and manifest-driven rather than commander: commander's diagnostics echo unknown option text, which spec §8 forbids. Errors come from a fixed catalogue; callers pick a code and can never pass a message, and faults are reported by argv position. Error envelope drops the fleet's `input` field (spec §8) and adds a stable `code`. Evidence (local, bun 1.3.14): `bun run check` exit 0, 28 pass / 0 fail. Positive controls: a planted argv echo in the failure path failed 12/13 non-disclosure tests; a planted ~/.ward write in `manifest` failed the HOME-sandbox test; both reverted and the suite re-ran green. Not yet pushed: origin does not exist until the operator creates the GitHub repo, so the PR and CI run are still owed before close.

Independent review (opum-workflow reviewer) of PR #1 found: (1, high) launching through bun loads the working directory's bunfig.toml and .env before main.ts runs, so a planted preload executes with argv in reach and a malformed bunfig is echoed. Filed as WCLI-16, now a dependency of WCLI-5 and WCLI-8; this PR drops package.json bin so nothing presents the source entry as a launcher. (2) Crash handlers were registered after imports; they now live in src/cli/guard.ts, which the new entry src/cli/ward.ts imports first. (3-4) --help is now a parser-level universal flag: it keeps --json, works on help itself, is answered before argument counts, and a value of -h stays a value. --list with a topic is a usage error. (5) Manifest lists resultKinds and exit 1 for every command. (6) Tests now: probe ~/.ward reads via an unreadable trap file (existence checks and stat are still not detected), run every rejected-argv case in process and through the entry, cover the guard for sync, timer and rejection throws, and assert the entry's import order; the vacuous catalogue test was removed and the layer check catches dynamic import(). Positive controls, each planted and then reverted: disabling guard registration failed 3 tests; a ~/.ward read in manifest failed the trap test; importing main before guard failed the import-order test.
finalSummary: Scaffolded the ward CLI contract and filed the P0 campaign (WCLI-1..16). Delivered: fleet result envelope; JSON diagnostics with a stable code and no input field, drawn from a fixed catalogue so no caller can put argv, exception or upstream text into an error; exit codes 0-7; a manifest-driven parser that reports faults by position; manifest, instructions, help and --version, none of which reads or writes ~/.ward; a guard that turns any escaped error into the fixed envelope; bun run check (tsc, biome, layer check, bun test). Verified in PR #1: bun run check exit 0 with 51 pass / 0 fail on bun 1.3.14 (macOS), and five positive controls, each failing its test when planted. An independent review's six findings were fixed in the same PR, except the launcher trust boundary, which is WCLI-16. CI: no checks configured on the repository yet, so none ran on PR #1; the evidence above is local.
